payload.title: 10 Lake Como Villas for an Exclusive-Use Wedding
payload.primary_keyword: lake como villa wedding exclusive use
payload.audience: Australian couples planning a luxury Lake Como wedding (AUD 150k+), comparing villas they can book exclusively for the whole celebration (assumed; not given by the person)
payload.reader: An Australian couple, early to mid 30s, budget around AUD 150k to 300k with parents contributing, 60 to 120 guests with most flying in from Australia, who have settled on Lake Como and now have a shortlist of villa names from Instagram and real weddings. They want to know which villas can actually be closed to everyone else for the whole weekend, whether their guests can sleep on site, what the house rules (minimum nights, music curfew, ceremony type) really are, and how to compare villas like for like before enquiring.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can check exclusive-use availability, house rules and costs (in AUD) for the couple's shortlisted Lake Como villas on their dates and guest count.
payload.angle: Page-one 'best Lake Como venues' lists mix hotels, museum gardens and private villas as if they were the same thing, and rarely say what you are actually booking. This guide only includes villas that can be booked for exclusive use of the property for a wedding (verified from each villa's official source by the planner-sme stage), and judges each one on the questions that decide a Lake Como weekend: does exclusive use include overnight rooms and how many guests sleep on site, the minimum night stay, the music curfew and where the party moves after it, whether a legal civil ceremony can happen on site or it must be symbolic with a town-hall ceremony elsewhere, seated versus standing capacity, private dock and boat access, and the wet-weather plan. It opens by defining 'exclusive use' plainly and closes with a like-for-like comparison table, so a couple can rule villas in or out before they enquire.
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words: what 'exclusive use' at a Lake Como villa usually means (the whole property, not just the event spaces), and that not every famous Lake Como venue offers it (hotels, and properties without bedrooms, are booked differently). Keep this general; specific exclusions only where planner-sme has verified them.

A plain-English 'What exclusive use actually covers' section: whole property and grounds closed to the public, overnight guests and how many rooms/beds, minimum nights (often a multi-night weekend), check-in/out and set-up/breakdown windows, music curfew and noise rules, what happens after curfew (indoor space, or move off site), outside caterers and suppliers (in-house or approved list), and ceremony type on site: legal civil ceremony only where the municipality authorises the location, otherwise symbolic on site plus civil or religious ceremony elsewhere. Link the Italy legal guide and the Lake Como legal guide. Every rule stated for a named villa needs a source; otherwise [[VERIFY]].

The 10 villas, each a real Lake Como villa confirmed from an official source (villa website, owner/management, or FAI for heritage properties) as bookable for exclusive use for a wedding. Do NOT include a villa that the planner-sme cannot verify; if fewer than 10 verify, flag to the orchestrator before the title is kept. Per villa, same fields in the same order: location on the lake (town, shore), seated dinner capacity vs standing reception capacity, rooms/guests sleeping on site, minimum nights, curfew/music rule, ceremony on site (civil legal / symbolic only / not confirmed), boat access and private dock, wet-weather option, one specific planner detail (e.g. where the aperitivo light falls, which terrace takes the dinner). Unsourced fields stay as [[VERIFY: ...]], never estimated.

How to compare villas: a like-for-like comparison table (villa, shore/town, seated, standing, sleeps on site, min nights, curfew, civil ceremony on site, private dock, wet-weather space). Explain why seated vs standing matters (the dinner sets your guest ceiling) and why rooms on site matter for an Australian guest list (fewer transfers, everyone together for the weekend, remaining guests need a nearby room block).

Getting there and around: nearest airports by name and that most guests will arrive via Milan, transfers, and that boats are part of the logistics (guest shuttles, the couple's arrival). Distances and travel times only if sourced; otherwise [[VERIFY]]. Note season and timing considerations (lake boat services, weather) only where sourced.
Where guests who do not fit in the villa stay: nearby hotel room blocks, and Wedded Privileges on every room booked through the Wedded Advisor (brand-facts claim, link /privileges).

Money talked about plainly but without unsigned figures: what typically drives the exclusive-use fee (season, day of week, nights, guest count, what is in-house) and link the Lake Como cost guide for ranges. Any AUD figure written 'From AUD ...' and flagged [[VERIFY: Nic sign-off]]; prefer no figure in this post.

Closing route to Wedded Concierge (live page /wonderland-concierge): one named Wedded Advisor checks exclusive-use availability and house rules for the couple's shortlist on their dates, quotes in AUD, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins and confirms inclusions in writing before the couple commits. Place the main invitation where a question has just been raised (after the comparison table) and once at the close.

Internal links: /destinations/europe/italy/lake-como-wedding (hub), /venue/villa-balbiano and /venue/villa-pizzo (only if those villas pass verification), /how-do-you-get-a-lake-como-wedding or the expert-advice legal guide (confirm canonical), /how-much-does-a-lake-como-wedding-cost (confirm canonical), /expert-advice/what-is-included-in-lake-como-wedding-packages, /expert-advice/getting-married-in-italy-the-complete-legal-guide-for-destination-couples, /privileges, /wonderland-concierge. Real weddings on our site held at a villa on the final list may be linked as 'see a real wedding here'.

FAQ (4 to 6): Can you get legally married at a Lake Como villa? How many nights do exclusive-use villas require? Is there a music curfew at Lake Como villas? Can all our guests stay at the villa? What happens if it rains? Is Villa d'Este (or another hotel) available for exclusive use? (answer only from verified sources).
avoid: Naming any villa, capacity, room count, minimum stay, curfew time, distance or price as fact without an official source. Use [[VERIFY: ...]].

Including hotels (e.g. Villa d'Este, Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni) or day-only heritage gardens/museums in the 10 unless an official source shows whole-property exclusive use for a wedding. They can be mentioned in a short 'why some famous names aren't on this list' note if verified.
Ranking villas as 'best' or ordering by prestige. Order by a stated logic (e.g. by shore or by guest size).
Celebrity name-dropping as the reason to choose a villa (existing site pages lean on this; this guide is about fit and rules).
Venue contact details, booking links or implying a partnership, exclusivity or preferred rates with any villa (brand-facts: enquiries go to Wedded Concierge; partner claims need checking).
Competitor wording, claims or images, including copy lifted from other 'Lake Como venues' listicles or villa marketing copy.
Clichés from the persona turn-offs: fairytale, dream day, breathtaking, say I do in paradise. No exclamation marks.
'No hidden costs' or 'all inclusive' claims; any bare price or non-AUD-only price.
Using AI-generated images of any real villa or Lake Como.
